spec.name: Daily reversal
spec.notes: Daily reversal on a few hundred names: buy yesterday's losers, sell the winners.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.7, annual return 10%, maximum drawdown 4%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.75 to -3.52 (change -6.26).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.75 to 2.75. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 0.10 (as submitted, 5 bps: 2.75); it breaks even at 10.2 bps with daily turnover 0.80.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.75 against 2.75 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is -1.20 against 2.75 in research, a gap of +3.95.
The best year gives 132% of total P&L (year 6) and calm regimes give -300%; Sharpe is 2.75 in calm and 3.07 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 36 distinct specs; the best of 36 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 2.36, so the claimed 2.70 becomes 0.34 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 85%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 5.39 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.01, 95th percentile 0.61).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.75 to as low as -3.52 (as low as 2.75 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 554% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 423% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

exhibits.summary: The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (lag_test EX-1, cost_test EX-3, holdout_test EX-5).
